sections.text: As a man can drink water from any side of a full tank, so the skilled theologian can wrest from any scripture that which will serve his purpose.
But thou hast only the right to work, but none to the fruit thereof. Let not then the fruit of thy action be thy motive; nor yet be thou enamored of inaction.
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
Perform all thy actions with mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.

We are now discussing Chapter 2, Sankhya Yoga, Yoga of Knowledge. So far we have seen that Bhagavan gave the knowledge of Sankhya. The Sankhya Darshan is Gina Darshan.
It takes us step by step what the reality is. From verse 11 through 30 he gave us this Tankhya Darshan, the Gnana Darshan. Then he said that now Ill teach you the Buddhi Yoga which is the application in your life, how to overcome the Prakruti.
So Sankhya Darshan says that Purusha and Prakruti are two separate entities. When Purusha gets involved with Prakruti, then all these problems start. The five kleshas start -- ragadvesha, etc.
So Yoga Shastra says how to overcome this entanglement with Prakriti. That Yoga Shastra, Bhagavan says, I will now teach you. But Bhagavan coined a new word: Buddhi Yoga -- Yoga which is established in wisdom.
So Bhagawan is basically now teaching Arjuna the Yoga Sastra in a very simple format that we all can understand. Arjun, I can understand. We all can understand.
We have touched upon a landmark verse in Bhagavad Gita -- verse 47 -- which is the most quoted verse in Bhagavad Gita. Most people quote this verse but only quote the first half of it. You will hardly ever hear anybody quoting the entire verse.
So the first line everybody is very familiar which says Karmanye vadhikarathe ma faleshu kadaa. And we quote that as if thats the instruction in reality, that is the statement of fact. The first line in that verse is statement of fact that you have only control over your actions, you do not have control over the fruits of actions.
Thats a statement of fact. All of us who can think about it will agree with that, that I can act or the results will come. Im not the Karma Falada.
Somebody else is either the world Bhagavan whoever you consider, but thats not you. But you do have control over actions. The second line is actually the prescription.
The second line is the advice which says Maa karma fala hai turbuhu. Never engage in any action with the expectations of the results. Its advice for us to be wise about how we act.
You will never be able to guess what the results will be. You will never have control over them. There is no reason for you to invest your energy into it.
Most of our energies are wasted in regrets of the past or in anxieties of the future, and then we have less enthusiasm in the present. So Bhagavan said, therefore, therefore, never engage in action with a result in your mind. And then the last portion of that verse is mate Sangahatu akarmani.
And never get attached to inaction by fear of failure or not having any clear direction. You do not want to get engaged in inaction. Instead it become tamasic.
So basically the advice Bhagavan has given is very clear. Engage in action without any expectations. Many commentators said this is where you change from prayers to shrayas.
So all Kamya karmas are for prayers. That which is going to be pleasant for me. Those actions which are not driven by the expectation of the fruits will lead you to Shreyas.
Because you will be only focusing on the action itself. So Bhagavan has given a clear direction and clear statement of the reality we live in. And now in the following verse, Bhagavan clearly demonstrate how one can engage in this activity.
Yogastha Kuru Karmani. Establish yourself in yoga. How to practice this Gnana Darshan, this knowledge of the true self.
As I said, there are two entities for Sankhya. Purusha who is always pure. Chaitanya but inactive.
Prakruti which is inert but active. Prakriti does not have the consciousness but it is very active. And Purusha which is pure consciousness but inactive.
When these two get entangled with each other, then the confusion starts. Maharishi Patanjalis Yoga Sutra said that Yoga Chitta Vritti Nirodha -- Yoga is to stop the modifications of your Chitta. The Chitta is like a mirror; it reflects the pure consciousness.
But there are Chitta Vrittis -- modifications which create this confusion. Basically the functions of Chitta in our day-to-day life include: Pramana (right knowledge), Viparyaya (contrary knowledge, wrong knowledge), Vikalpa (doubt), Nidra (sleep or Tamas), and then Smriti (memory). These five modifications of Chitta create flickering in our Chitta.
They do not let the consciousness reflect purely. Once these Vrittis are negated, the Purusha is reflected through the Chitta in its pure form -- that is basically what the Yoga Shastra says. But this is very complicated for an average person to understand.
So Bhagavan is now clarifying this in very simple terms which you and I can understand and try to practice. Yogastha Kuru Karmani: you have to establish yourself in yoga, then act outside. If you are not established in yoga then actions will be haphazard.
They will be driven by the results. Then obviously there will be all the side effects which come along with it. Sangam tyaktva Dhananjaya this is the most important part of this verse and most people leave that out.
Sangam tyaksva act in this world by establishing yourself in yoga and without any attachment. So even attachment to actions themselves in is detrimental. If I get too attached -- I have to do this, I need to do this -- then it will be problematic.
There may not be an opportunity for those particular actions. In other words, you should perform the actions which are appropriate, necessary, and available in that environment, and not insist on the particular actions youre attached to: I will only do this but I will not do anything else. In olden society in India, a Brahmin could only do certain work. He could not do menial work.
And I know in times where there was not enough work, people suffered because they would not say, I will do this other work if my usual work is not available. Bhagawan said: dont get attached to actions. Whatever actions are available and appropriate, engage yourself in them. No attachment to what type of actions Im performing -- I also have to establish myself in yoga.
Now, when an average person hears the word yoga, he gets really frightened. You want me to become a yogi? He will say, Oh no, no, I dont want to become a yogi. I have my own life to live. I want to say: no, no, thats not what Yoga is all about. Yoga is something different.
So what Maharishi Patanjali says as Chitta Vritti Nirodhaha, Bhagavan puts in a very different way which is very palatable to us. He said: Siddhi Asiddhi Samo Bhatva -- become even-minded to success and failure. Once again, going back to the previous verse, success and failure come from past actions.
The success and failures which I am experiencing now are actually results of my past actions. I have no control whatsoever on them anymore. I should have gone to medical college and I would have been a doctor and made more money and Id be considered a frontline worker right now.
I cannot change that. And therefore, whatever the results Im facing right now, whether I consider them to be success or kind of failures, I should be even minded, take them as they are without attaching my likings and dislikings. Siddhi Asiddhi Samo Bhutva Samatvam Yoga Uchate -- the very first definition in Bhagavad Gita about Yoga: Samatvam Yoga Uchate.
We will see more definitions, and therefore this chapter is so important. These next three or four verses starting from 47 are so loaded with meaning -- they compress all the wisdom of Sankhya and Yoga into these few verses -- that we have to pay a lot of attention to understand them. Bhagavan said Siddhi Asiddhi Samo Bhatva: in a sense, do not pay attention to what you are getting because of your past actions.
Treat them equally, with Prasada Buddhi. Engage in your present actions. Do not let your present actions get affected by the Siddhi or Asiddhi which you are facing right now.
Samatvam Yoga Uchate -- the balance of mind is Yoga. So we go back to what Maharishi Patanjali said. Yoga Chitta Vritti Nirodha.
When Chitta is agitated by all these Vrittis -- right knowledge, contrary knowledge, memories, Nidra, Tamas -- all those Vrittis are creating impurities in Chitta. That Chitta is then not available to reflect the right knowledge, the right reality of who I am. Bhagawan said Samatvam Yoga: this balance of mind which does not get affected either by the past or by anxiety of the future, which does not lose any enthusiasm in the present or in your current actions -- that is Yoga.
Once you are established in this, your actions will bear right results. In the next verse, how to look at the situation: Durena Hi Avaram Karma Buddhi Yogat Dhananjaya. Actions which are prompted by desires are far lower than Buddhi Yoga.
Bhagawan is using a very unique term -- Buddhi Yoga. Buddhi Yoga is Yoga of wisdom, an intelligent way of living, establishing yourself in Buddhi. So again, we have discussed before that Chitta is a thinking entity.
The thinking entity has several functions. We know the three functions are Manas, Buddhi, and Ahankar. The Ahankar is always constant -- the I feeling is always constant.
When that thinking entity is in doubt, it is mind. Sankalpa Vikalpatmaka Manah. But Nischayatmika Buddhi -- Buddhi which is decisive: this is right, this is the truth, and this is what I should be working on. Once you establish yourself in that Buddhi, that wisdom of what is right and what is wrong, and you are not in that doubtful situation -- that is Buddhi Yoga.
When Chitta is in that Nischayatmika mode, its Buddhi. So Bhagavan said, engage yourself in Buddhi Yoga. That Buddhi Yoga is far better than Karma.
And here Karma is only Kamya Karma. Desire prompted actions. Karma Khanda, all the actions all the way up to the desire to get Swarga is all Kamya Karma.
Therefore all actions perform for those results. Bhagwan said anytime. Even though they may be the highest form of actions to achieve the best possible state of living or living standard, they are far lower than Buddhi Yoga.
Buddhau Sharanam Anviccha -- take refuge in Buddhi. This also reminded me of Buddham Sharanam Gacchami, Dhammam Sharanam Gacchami, Sangham Sharanam Gacchami. I take refuge in Buddha, in the wisdom of Buddha. Here Bhagavan says: take refuge in your own wisdom.
Buddhau Sharanam Anviccha. Kripanaha Phala Hetavah -- those who are working in this world to get conducive results, or to get the fruits of their actions all the way up to reaching the heavens. They are Kripanaha -- unfortunate misers.
The translation is wretched. Kripana means miser. A miser is always unfortunate because he never gets to enjoy his own wealth. He has all the wealth but cant enjoy it, so hes wretched.
Those unfortunate people -- and that includes all of us who are working for the fruits of actions. They are very unfortunate because they will never be able to enjoy fruits of their actions. They will always be in misery, either regretting the past or anxious about the future.
They will never be living in present. They are always living in future or in past. They both are hypothetical situation.
There is no past that I have experienced and there is no future that I have seen. Anytime I experience, it is always present. Bhagavan says those people are really unfortunate misers who waste their energies into past and in future and completely ignores the present.
O shantihi shri gurubyonamaha harihio. So we had been discussing Chapter 2, Sankhya Yoga, Yoga of Knowledge. And so far we have seen that Bhagavan gave us the knowledge of the Sankhya which is teaching us that this self is immortal, this body is mortal.

Verse 47 is the most famous verse of the Gita: Thou hast only the right to work, but none to the fruit thereof. Let not then the fruit of thy action be thy motive; nor yet be thou enamored of inaction. This is not advice but a statement of fact: we control our actions but not their results, which depend on countless factors beyond us. The prescription follows: do not let results motivate your action, and do not use uncertainty of results as an excuse for inaction.
Verse 48 gives the positive instruction: Perform all thy actions with mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity. The definition Samatvam Yoga Uchyate - Equanimity is Yoga - transforms our understanding of spiritual practice from something done on a meditation cushion to a quality of mind maintained throughout all activity.
Today, choose one action - perhaps your work, a conversation, or a household task - and practice Karma Yoga with it. Before beginning, consciously set your intention: I will do this to the best of my ability, as an offering, without attachment to the outcome. During the action, stay focused on the task itself rather than imagining future results. Afterward, accept whatever comes with equanimity. Notice: Does releasing attachment to results make you more or less effective? More or less peaceful? This is the laboratory where the Gitas teaching is tested.
